scope: Research only: tension, uncertainty and meaningful friction in instrument/office horror; no gameplay architecture, new mechanics, implementation edits or playtest claims.

method.source_selection: Six curated developer essays/interviews, using full source text or publisher transcript rather than search snippets. Quotes were checked mechanically against saved retrieved text.
method.payment: No paid APIs, API-key setup or paid transcript service used.
method.epistemic_labels: Direct claims are attributed source statements. Dead Wire inferences and pitfalls are explicitly untested extrapolations, not facts about current game behavior.
method.independence: The two Thomas Grip essays are one developer viewpoint, not independent corroboration. SOMA audio is a separate specialist account; Szymanski, Mobius designers and Pope supply additional viewpoints.
not_performed: Listening to or watching the Szymanski interview

provided_dead_wire_context.provenance: Supplied task context only; not independently inspected or verified.
provided_dead_wire_context.m1: One 1894 telegraph office and three transmissions.
provided_dead_wire_context.hook: The operator hears WATER, while the hand writes WATCHER.
provided_dead_wire_context.evidence_boundary: Objective Morse/tape immutable; perception and transcript separate.
provided_dead_wire_context.tension: Split attention among work, window, door and evidence verification, not monster combat or constant jumpscares.
provided_dead_wire_context.existing_beats: Ordinary/quiet introduction; delayed calls at 20/38/50 seconds; paper inspection and filing; lamp wick and register winding.
provided_dead_wire_context.canon: Listener cannot move physical objects; observation changes only between observations.

sources.title: Dusk and the Art of Making Short Games with David Szymanski
sources.author_or_interview: David Szymanski, interviewed by Joe Nash
sources.access_method: direct HTTPS text retrieval after extractor failed
sources.read_scope: Full transcript retrieved; relevant horror/embodiment/audio sections at 00:03:48, 00:11:25, 00:15:25–00:21:30 read. Video/audio was not watched or listened to.

short_excerpts.text: I want you to be in this world and in this experience as a human character. Not as a submarine.
short_excerpts.speaker: David Szymanski
short_excerpts.location: 00:15:25–00:18:14, Szymanski answer on the first-person controller

short_excerpts.text: they're forced to keep moving around in the sub and they're forced to be turning their view and then hearing sounds from different sides
short_excerpts.speaker: David Szymanski
short_excerpts.location: Same answer, physical movement and directional sound

short_excerpts.text: you can go to any random point on the map and take a picture. And what you're seeing is actually what's out there so to speak.
short_excerpts.speaker: David Szymanski
short_excerpts.location: 00:20:53, Szymanski answer on the real external world

direct_claims.text: Szymanski says direct submarine control would shift the player’s avatar away from a vulnerable human; bodily movement and changes of view/sound direction make confinement perceptible.[10]
He states that photographs at arbitrary coordinates show the actual external game world, despite the separated camera/interior implementation.[10]

dead_wire_inferences.text: For Dead Wire’s existing work/window/door split, physical reorientation has a legible attention cost; it need not be implemented as delayed or dropped input.
dead_wire_inferences.status: researcher inference, not a developer claim or tested result

dead_wire_inferences.text: Restricted access to a trustworthy view is different from an arbitrarily false view; Iron Lung provides a useful analogy for limited observation with dependable underlying evidence.
dead_wire_inferences.status: researcher inference, not a developer claim or tested result

dead_wire_pitfalls.text: Do not read Iron Lung’s cumbersome situation as evidence that mouse lag, ignored clicks or sticky inspection are desirable; this interview argues for embodiment, not latency.
dead_wire_pitfalls.status: inferred risk, not an observed Dead Wire defect

dead_wire_pitfalls.text: Do not infer that every photograph or every future instrument channel must lie in order to sustain uncertainty; Szymanski explicitly describes world-grounded photographs.
dead_wire_pitfalls.status: inferred risk, not an observed Dead Wire defect

sources.limits: No input-latency measurement, optimal interaction duration or proof of Dead Wire effectiveness is provided. Published transcript has occasional transcription errors; quoted wording is preserved.

sources.title: 9 Years, 9 Lessons on Horror
sources.developer_role: Frictional Games co-founder and creative director
sources.source_type: Developer-authored retrospective on the studio website
sources.access_method: web_extract full article; raw HTML for byline/date
sources.read_scope: Full essay read, especially Lessons 1, 3, 4, 6, 7 and 9.

short_excerpts.text: spacing the scares apart made players much more scared than previously.
short_excerpts.speaker: Thomas Grip
short_excerpts.location: Lesson 3: Scares alone won’t make a horror game

short_excerpts.text: It’s when there is a gap in our knowledge, a certain amount of uncertainty, that horror can really shine.
short_excerpts.speaker: Thomas Grip

short_excerpts.text: If the game is constantly engaging the player with thinking about their aim, checking ammo, and looking for loot, there’s no room left for much else.
short_excerpts.speaker: Thomas Grip
short_excerpts.location: Lesson 4: Fun gameplay is just too… fun

direct_claims.text: Grip reports that reducing the Amnesia study’s many jumpscares and emphasizing the castle mysteries made the section scarier.[9]
He argues that incomplete knowledge can sustain horror, while an attention-heavy gameplay loop leaves less capacity for frightening interpretation.[9]

dead_wire_inferences.text: A quiet, comprehensible office baseline and room for interpretation are compatible with the existing three-transmission scope; constant incident density is not required.
dead_wire_inferences.status: researcher inference, not a developer claim or tested result

dead_wire_inferences.text: The uncertainty appropriate to a threat need not apply to how a work control registers input or to the identity of an already preserved record.
dead_wire_inferences.status: researcher inference, not a developer claim or tested result

dead_wire_pitfalls.text: Too many simultaneous lamp, winding, paper and warning demands could consume the attention needed to notice and interpret the WATER/WATCHER discrepancy.
dead_wire_pitfalls.status: inferred risk, not an observed Dead Wire defect

dead_wire_pitfalls.text: Adding a loud scare to every delayed call risks teaching a predictable scare schedule rather than sustaining uncertainty.
dead_wire_pitfalls.status: inferred risk, not an observed Dead Wire defect

dead_wire_pitfalls.text: Keep it vague is not permission to contradict the supplied immutable Morse/tape rule or Listener’s no-physical-object-movement rule.
dead_wire_pitfalls.status: inferred risk, not an observed Dead Wire defect

sources.limits: These are studio observations and design arguments, not controlled studies. The essay does not validate 20/38/50-second waits, three calls, or any universal safe scare frequency.

sources.title: Thoughts On Inside and Playable Stories
sources.developer_role: Frictional Games co-founder and creative director; external analysis of Inside, not a Playdead postmortem
sources.source_type: Developer-authored critical design essay on the studio website
sources.access_method: web_extract full article; raw HTML for byline/date
sources.read_scope: Full essay read; puzzle planning, consistent affordances, trial-and-error and filler sections used.

short_excerpts.text: The player just needs to know: the boundaries that are in place, that the problem is solvable, and what goal state to strive for.
short_excerpts.speaker: Thomas Grip
short_excerpts.location: Puzzle discussion: solvability and goal state

short_excerpts.text: Any time it feels like you need to guess what the designer is thinking, or are being handheld along a set course, you’ve got a bad puzzle.
short_excerpts.speaker: Thomas Grip

short_excerpts.text: Problems tend to arise when this trial-and-error becomes an integral part of the moment-to-moment gameplay, or when it interferes with the control of the player character.
short_excerpts.speaker: Thomas Grip

direct_claims.text: Grip argues that a puzzle needs comprehensible boundaries, solvability and a target state so the player can form and execute plans.[3]
He distinguishes discovery from guessing the designer’s intention, and warns against trial-and-error interfering with moment-to-moment character control.[3]

dead_wire_inferences.text: Uncertainty about a message’s meaning can coexist with certainty about how inspection, filing and winding behave.
dead_wire_inferences.status: researcher inference, not a developer claim or tested result

dead_wire_inferences.text: Meaningful friction here means understandable effort or commitment that changes attention or information; input lag means the player’s intended action fails to arrive predictably. This distinction is a synthesis, not a quoted technical definition.
dead_wire_inferences.status: researcher inference, not a developer claim or tested result

dead_wire_pitfalls.text: If paper pickup, inspection or filing is ambiguous, players may diagnose a UI defect rather than doubt their perception.
dead_wire_pitfalls.status: inferred risk, not an observed Dead Wire defect

dead_wire_pitfalls.text: Repeated maintenance without an information, attention or narrative consequence can become filler; this essay critiques repeated puzzles that add no story value.
dead_wire_pitfalls.status: inferred risk, not an observed Dead Wire defect

dead_wire_pitfalls.text: A forced loss of control for WATCHER risks feeling like authorial override if players cannot distinguish the written transcript from the preserved received signal.
dead_wire_pitfalls.status: inferred risk, not an observed Dead Wire defect

sources.limits: Grip is interpreting another studio’s game, not reporting Playdead’s intent. The essay is not an input-latency experiment; the friction/lag distinction above is inferred.

sources.title: SOMA – Behind The Sound
sources.author_or_interview: Samuel Justice; embedded first-person account from Kpow Audio
sources.developer_role: SOMA audio director and dialogue implementation team
sources.source_type: First-hand audio-production essay on the studio website
sources.access_method: web_extract full article; raw HTML for date
sources.read_scope: Full essay read, including the Kpow Audio signal-path and historical-blackbox sections.

short_excerpts.text: if we were to turn off the visuals, you could instantly tell where you were.
short_excerpts.speaker: Samuel Justice

short_excerpts.text: The audio team have done an amazing job at creating an audio environment that balances impact and authenticity
short_excerpts.speaker: Kpow Audio, quoted within Justice’s essay
short_excerpts.location: Kpow Audio: voiceover implementation and processing

short_excerpts.text: we tried – wherever possible – to recreate the signal paths described on screen.
short_excerpts.speaker: Kpow Audio, quoted within Justice’s essay
short_excerpts.location: Kpow Audio: recreating depicted signal paths

direct_claims.text: Justice describes designing contrasting sonic spaces that remain recognizable even with the visuals disabled.[4]
Kpow Audio describes balancing impact with authenticity and reproducing the signal paths depicted by in-world equipment.[4]

dead_wire_inferences.text: For existing Dead Wire signals, recognizable source and carrier behavior can support verification even when their perceived content becomes uncertain.
dead_wire_inferences.status: researcher inference, not a developer claim or tested result

dead_wire_inferences.text: Mechanical dirt and atmosphere have to coexist with readable evidence-bearing timing/content; the need to protect Morse intelligibility is our application, not a SOMA mixing rule stated in this essay.
dead_wire_inferences.status: researcher inference, not a developer claim or tested result

dead_wire_pitfalls.text: Static, drones, wind and machine sounds that mask evidence-bearing signal timing could make WATER/WATCHER an audio-decoding accident rather than a meaningful discrepancy.
dead_wire_pitfalls.status: inferred risk, not an observed Dead Wire defect

dead_wire_pitfalls.text: An unsettling sound that has no distinguishable source or consistent carrier may undercut instrument trust instead of deepening contextual uncertainty.
dead_wire_pitfalls.status: inferred risk, not an observed Dead Wire defect

dead_wire_pitfalls.text: Do not import SOMA’s recording volume, binaural requirements or signal-processing stack as necessary scope for a single office.
dead_wire_pitfalls.status: inferred risk, not an observed Dead Wire defect

sources.limits: The essay documents production techniques, not a controlled intelligibility test. It specifies no loudness target, EQ band, ducking rule or Morse decoding threshold.

sources.title: Live, die, repeat: How Outer Wilds piques curiosity in an ambivalent solar system
sources.author_or_interview: Kris Graft interviewing Alex Beachum and Loan Verneau
sources.developer_role: Outer Wilds designers speaking about their own development process
sources.source_type: Reported interview with direct developer quotations
sources.access_method: extractor returned only a partial article; full public HTML retrieved and article paragraphs parsed
sources.read_scope: Full article body read after recovering the omitted curiosity/playtest sections; only developer quotations treated as primary claims.

short_excerpts.text: the only thing you can bring back in time with you is your memories.
short_excerpts.speaker: Alex Beachum
short_excerpts.location: Alex Beachum: memories and the time loop

short_excerpts.text: That [object from space] is not new to them to them [when] everything is new.
short_excerpts.speaker: Alex Beachum

short_excerpts.text: you can't expect someone to be curious about something specific unless they're already familiar with everything in their immediate vicinity.
short_excerpts.speaker: Alex Beachum

direct_claims.text: Beachum explains that the time loop privileges memories/knowledge as the persistent value of exploration.[8]
He reports that an early meteor opening failed to provoke curiosity because players did not yet know the normal village, and states that local familiarity is needed for specific curiosity.[8]

dead_wire_inferences.text: Dead Wire’s ordinary introduction matters because the player needs a learned normal before a discrepant transcript becomes a specific anomaly.
dead_wire_inferences.status: researcher inference, not a developer claim or tested result

dead_wire_inferences.text: The existing record comparison can count as progress when it produces actionable understanding, not merely another completed filing gesture.
dead_wire_inferences.status: researcher inference, not a developer claim or tested result

dead_wire_pitfalls.text: Opening with anomalies everywhere could erase the comparison baseline and turn a precise discrepancy into generic strangeness.
dead_wire_pitfalls.status: inferred risk, not an observed Dead Wire defect

dead_wire_pitfalls.text: Finishing three routine submissions is not by itself evidence of knowledge-based progression; this report cannot establish whether the player has learned anything consequential.
dead_wire_pitfalls.status: inferred risk, not an observed Dead Wire defect

dead_wire_pitfalls.text: Outer Wilds’ continuously changing world is not license to break Dead Wire’s supplied rule that observation changes only between observations.
dead_wire_pitfalls.status: inferred risk, not an observed Dead Wire defect

sources.limits: Outer Wilds is an analogy for discovery, not focused office horror. The interview supports familiarity and knowledge-value principles, not transplanting its world scale or time-loop architecture.

sources.title: Interrogating detective mechanics with a real-life detective
sources.author_or_interview: Sean Martin interviewing Lucas Pope and Adam Richardson
sources.developer_role: Lucas Pope: Return of the Obra Dinn creator; Richardson: detective, not a game developer
sources.source_type: Reported interview with direct developer quotations
sources.access_method: extractor omitted key developer passages; full public HTML retrieved and article paragraphs parsed
sources.read_scope: Full article body read; selected claims below are Lucas Pope’s, not Richardson’s or the journalist’s.

short_excerpts.text: Defining those limits early helped me to focus on how to structure the overall narrative and progression to keep it understandable and revelatory.
short_excerpts.speaker: Lucas Pope

short_excerpts.text: different players can find and interpret different clues and still progress similarly.
short_excerpts.speaker: Lucas Pope

direct_claims.text: Pope credits the bounded observe-and-note loop with keeping narrative/progression understandable and revelatory.[12]
He explains that clues can contribute globally, letting players find and interpret different evidence while still progressing.[12]

dead_wire_inferences.text: Comparison has value when evidence can constrain a hypothesis; the separate objective Morse/tape and subjective perception/transcript layers are a promising supplied premise for that distinction, not proof of a successful implementation.
dead_wire_inferences.status: researcher inference, not a developer claim or tested result

dead_wire_inferences.text: An incorrect interpretation is different from arbitrary alteration of the facts used to reason; the present immutable-evidence requirement supplies that boundary.
dead_wire_inferences.status: researcher inference, not a developer claim or tested result

dead_wire_pitfalls.text: If every retained record can silently rewrite, comparison no longer constrains interpretations and deduction risks becoming guessing.
dead_wire_pitfalls.status: inferred risk, not an observed Dead Wire defect

dead_wire_pitfalls.text: Do not import Obra Dinn’s sixty-person scale or automatic fate-confirmation system; this article does not support a specific confirmation cadence for Dead Wire.
dead_wire_pitfalls.status: inferred risk, not an observed Dead Wire defect

dead_wire_pitfalls.text: Do not attribute the interview’s claims about real investigative practice to Pope; the detective and developer speak in separate roles.
dead_wire_pitfalls.status: inferred risk, not an observed Dead Wire defect

sources.limits: Pope discusses a deliberately bounded logic puzzle, not unreliable perception horror. The article does not state that evidence immutability is a universal design law; that application is ours. Three-fate confirmation is not used as evidence here.

cross_source_inferences.text: The strongest shared distinction is uncertainty about interpretation or threat versus reliability of action and retained evidence; conflating them risks converting dread into interface confusion.
cross_source_inferences.status: synthesis; not a universal law established by the sources

cross_source_inferences.text: Quietness needs a comprehensible normal and a reason to attend; it is neither a licence for undirected idle waiting nor a requirement to fill every pause with a scare.
cross_source_inferences.status: synthesis; exact Dead Wire call timings remain unvalidated

cross_source_inferences.text: The existing WATER/WATCHER premise depends on perceivable disagreement between channels. Obscuring the received signal beyond verification, or silently changing the retained tape, would remove the supplied factual anchor.
Existing office actions can occupy attention, but a continuous checklist of equally urgent chores could leave no mental room to interpret the window, door or signal.
cross_source_inferences.status: inferred attention-budget risk, not an observed game defect

cross_source_inferences.text: Knowledge progression requires a consequence for understanding; merely completing the three transmissions cannot establish that criterion without actual game observation or testing.
cross_source_inferences.status: research limitation; no new progression design proposed
